move.title: Mastery: mash, mix, test
move.body: This is the unit's mastery week. You'll make banana bread while an adult watches but doesn't help: mash ripe bananas, mix the batter just until the flour disappears, and decide for yourself when it's done with a toothpick.

callback.body: Your muffins were mixed in two bowls and tested with a toothpick. Banana bread uses the same steps in one bowl, and bakes much longer because a loaf is so much thicker.

why.title: Very ripe bananas
why.body: Bananas with lots of brown spots are sweeter and softer. They mash smooth and make the bread moist and full of flavor.

why.title: Mix just until
why.body: Stirring flour builds gluten, which makes quick bread tough. Stop as soon as no dry flour shows.

why.title: Baking soda
why.body: Bananas and brown sugar are a little acidic. Baking soda reacts with them and makes bubbles that raise the loaf.

why.title: The toothpick test
why.body: A loaf bakes from the outside in, so the center is last. A toothpick pushed into the middle that comes out clean, or with a few moist crumbs, means it's done.

wrong.sign: The top is brown but the toothpick is wet
wrong.fix: Lay foil loosely over the top and bake 5 more minutes. Test again.

wrong.sign: The loaf sank in the middle
wrong.fix: It came out too soon. Test the very center next time.
It was stirred too much. Stop as soon as the flour is gone.
Run the butter knife around the edges before turning it out.

quiz.q: Which bananas make the best bread?
choices: Very ripe, with lots of brown spots

quiz.q: Where do you test with the toothpick?
choices: The very center of the loaf

quiz.q: The toothpick has wet batter. What do you do?
choices: Bake 5 more minutes and test again
quiz.explain: Foil keeps the top from getting too dark.

ingredients.text: a little more, soft, for the pan

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Brush the loaf pan with soft butter.
steps.look: The whole pan shiny with butter.

steps.text: Melt the 6 tablespoons of butter in the small bowl in the microwave.
steps.tip: Let it cool while you mash.

steps.text: Peel the bananas into the large bowl. Mash them with the fork.
steps.look: Mostly smooth, with a few small lumps.

steps.text: Stir in the melted butter, brown sugar, egg, and vanilla.
steps.look: Smooth, with no streaks of egg.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshell.
Sprinkle the baking soda, salt, and cinnamon over the top. Stir them in.
steps.tip: Rub the baking soda between your fingers so there are no lumps.

steps.text: Spoon and level the flour into the bowl. Stir just until no dry flour shows.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw batter. It has raw egg.

steps.text: Scrape the batter into the pan and smooth the top.
steps.look: An even layer, corner to corner.

steps.text: Bake until the top is deep golden and cracked.
steps.look: Deep golden, with a crack down the middle.
steps.tip: Getting too dark? Lay foil loosely on top.

steps.text: With oven mitts, pull out the rack. Push a toothpick into the very center of the loaf.

target.look: A clean toothpick, or a few moist crumbs, from the center

steps.tip: Wet batter? Bake 5 more minutes and test again.

steps.text: Turn off the oven. Cool the loaf in the pan 10 minutes. Run the butter knife around it and turn it out.
steps.tip: Let it cool more before slicing.

wet.text: Separate the eggs: crack each one and pass the yolk back and forth between the half shells over the medium bowl, letting the white drip into the bowl. Drop the yolks into the bananas. Then stir in the melted butter, brown sugar, and vanilla.
wet.look: Smooth, with no streaks of egg.
wet.tip: Not a speck of yolk can get into the whites, or they won't whip. If a yolk breaks, save that egg for breakfast and use another.

soda.text: Sprinkle the salt and cinnamon over the top. Stir them in.

flour.text: Spoon and level the flour into the bowl. Stir just until no dry flour shows.

add.text: Wash and dry the whisk. Whisk the egg whites in the medium bowl hard and fast until they're white, foamy, and hold soft peaks.
add.look: When you lift the whisk, the foam stands up in a peak that flops over at the tip.
add.tip: Take turns: it's hard work. An electric hand mixer is faster, if you have one.

add.text: Scoop the whites onto the batter in the large bowl. Fold them in gently with the spatula: cut down through the middle, sweep along the bottom, and turn the batter over the top. Turn the bowl and repeat until no white streaks are left.
add.look: A light, fluffy batter with no white streaks.
add.tip: Don't taste the raw batter. It has raw egg and raw flour.

move.title: Mastery: mash, mix, test
move.body: This is the unit's mastery week. You'll make banana bread while an adult watches but doesn't help: mash ripe bananas, mix the batter just until the flour disappears, fold in whipped egg whites to lift it, and decide for yourself when it's done with a toothpick. With no raising agent, it bakes into a denser, moister loaf.

wrong.sign: The top is brown but the toothpick is wet
wrong.fix: Lay foil loosely over the top and bake 5 more minutes. Test again.

wrong.sign: The loaf sank in the middle
wrong.fix: It came out too soon. Test the very center next time.
It was stirred too much. Stop as soon as the flour is gone.
Run the butter knife around the edges before turning it out.
The whites weren't whipped long enough, or they were stirred in instead of folded. Next time, whip to soft peaks and fold gently.

add.title: Whipped whites lift it
add.body: Egg whites whisked hard trap thousands of tiny air bubbles. Folded gently into the batter, the bubbles swell in the hot oven and lift it a little. Stir hard and they pop, so fold, don't stir. It bakes a little denser than with a raising agent, and that's fine.
